item.text:
{"source":"import Base

# B3/S23 asks for three in either view: the ring, or the ring plus its center.
def Life.three(cell: U32, +ring: U32) -> U32:
  Bool.to_u32(
    Bool.or(
      U32.is_eq(ring, 3),
      U32.is_eq((ring + cell : U32), 3)))

# Cut the flat board into rows and cap every row with dead cells.
def Life.halo(
  height: Nat,
  +width: Nat,
  +cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, List<&2, U32>>:
  match height:
    case 0n:
      Nil{}
    case 1n+rest:
      (0 <> List.append(
        &2,
        U32,
        List.take(&2, U32, cells, width),
        [0])) <>
        Life.halo(
          rest,
          width,
          List.drop(&2, U32, cells, width))

# Three columns advance together across three haloed rows.
def Life.focus(
  +north: List<&2, U32>,
  +middle: List<&2, U32>,
  +south: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match north middle south:
    case nw <> +north1 w <> +middle1 sw <> +south1:
      match north1 middle1 south1:
        case n <> north2 cell <> middle2 s <> south2:
          match north2 middle2 south2:
            case ne <> nt e <> mt se <> st:
              +ring = (
                nw + n + ne
                + w + e
                + sw + s + se : U32)
              Life.three(cell, ring) <>
                Life.focus(north1, middle1, south1)
            case _ _ _:
              Nil{}
        case _ _ _:
          Nil{}
    case _ _ _:
      Nil{}

# The same three-wide focus advances one row at a time down the haloed board.
def Life.sweep(
  +rows: List<&2, List<&2, U32>>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match rows:
    case Nil{}:
      Nil{}
    case north <> tail:
      match tail:
        case Nil{}:
          Nil{}
        case middle <> after:
          match after:
            case Nil{}:
              Nil{}
            case south <> rest:
              List.append(
                &2,
                U32,
                Life.focus(north, middle, south),
                Life.sweep(tail))

def step(
  width: U32,
  height: U32,
  cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  +w = U32.to_nat(width)
  h = U32.to_nat(height)
  +dead = List.replicate(U32, Nat.add(w, 2n), 0)
  Life.sweep(
    dead <>
      List.append(
        &2,
        List<&2, U32>,
        Life.halo(h, w, cells),
        [dead]))

def evolve(
  turns: Nat,
  +width: U32,
  +height: U32,
  cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match turns:
    case 0n:
      cells
    case 1n+rest:
      evolve(rest, width, height, step(width, height, cells))
","hypothesis":"Represent the board as a dead-haloed nested tape. Horizontal triples move across three rows while the same three-wide focus moves vertically across the row tape. B3/S23 then collapses to one relation: exactly three either around the cell or including its center. Marking the retained row tails reusable permits each to be inspected for the current window and then reused as the structurally smaller recursive state.","findings":"Confirmed: the round-1 implementation passed all reported behavior and semantic checks. Confirmed style weakness: separate peeking, accumulator-driven row splitting, and scattered boundary defaults obscured the shared sliding-window structure; this revision replaces them with one explicit halo and symmetric horizontal and vertical three-wide sweeps. Confirmed compiler finding: `Life.focus` consumed each first tail while inspecting it and later reused that tail for recursion. The repair marks `north1`, `middle1`, and `south1` reusable in the outer pattern, preserving the intended algorithm and structural descent."}
